name: Contradiction Matrix (TRIZ)
whenToUse: When two different engineering parameters are in conflict — improving one degrades the other — and the matrix should name the proven solution principles for that pair; not when a single parameter itself would have to hold two opposite values, which is what the physical contradiction is for.
problemPlaceholder: e.g. The support structure must become stronger — but then becomes too heavy.
hintSelectBoth: Pick both parameters to see recommendations.
warnSameParameter: Improving and worsening parameters are identical — no contradiction.
noContradiction: No recommendation registered for this combination in the standard matrix.
matrixLegend: Row = improving (↑), column = worsening (↓). Cell number = count of recommended principles. Click a cell to apply the selection.

1.name: Weight of moving object
1.description: Mass of an object that moves freely in a gravitational field.

2.name: Weight of stationary object
2.description: Mass of an object that does not move.

3.name: Length of moving object
3.description: Any linear dimension (not necessarily the longest) of a moving object.

4.name: Length of stationary object
4.description: Any linear dimension of a stationary object.

5.name: Area of moving object
5.description: Two-dimensional measure of a surface or a section of a moving object.

6.name: Area of stationary object
6.description: Two-dimensional measure of a surface or section of a stationary object.

7.name: Volume of moving object
7.description: Cubic measure of space occupied by a moving object.

8.name: Volume of stationary object
8.description: Cubic measure of space occupied by a stationary object.

9.name: Speed
9.description: Velocity of an object or rate of a process or action in time.

10.name: Force
10.description: Any interaction intended to change an object's condition.

11.name: Stress or pressure
11.description: Force per unit area; also, tension.

12.name: Shape
12.description: External contours or appearance of a system.

13.name: Stability of object's composition
13.description: Wholeness or integrity of the system; ability to resist decomposition.

14.name: Strength
14.description: Resistance to changing in response to force; resistance to breaking.

15.name: Duration of action by moving object
15.description: Time during which a moving object performs its function (service life).

16.name: Duration of action by stationary object
16.description: Service life of a stationary object.

17.name: Temperature
17.description: Thermal condition of the object or system.

18.name: Illumination intensity
18.description: Light flux per unit area; brightness or quality of light.

19.name: Use of energy by moving object
19.description: Energy consumed by a moving object.

20.name: Use of energy by stationary object
20.description: Energy consumed by a stationary object.

21.name: Power
21.description: Time rate at which work is performed.

22.name: Loss of energy
22.description: Energy that does not contribute to the job done.

23.name: Loss of substance
23.description: Partial or complete, permanent or temporary loss of material.

24.name: Loss of information
24.description: Partial or complete, permanent or temporary loss of data or access to data.

25.name: Loss of time
25.description: Time inefficiency; lost or wasted time.

26.name: Quantity of substance
26.description: Number or amount of a system's materials, substances, parts, or subsystems.

27.name: Reliability
27.description: Ability to perform intended functions in predictable ways and conditions.

28.name: Measurement accuracy
28.description: Closeness of a measured value to the actual value of the property.

29.name: Manufacturing precision
29.description: Extent to which the actual characteristic matches the specified one.

30.name: Object-affecting harmful factors
30.description: External factors that degrade or damage the object.

31.name: Object-generated harmful factors
31.description: Harmful effects developed by the object as part of its operation.

32.name: Ease of manufacture
32.description: How easy or convenient it is to manufacture the system.

33.name: Ease of operation
33.description: Simplicity in using and controlling the system.

34.name: Ease of repair
34.description: Simplicity, time, and convenience of repair.

35.name: Adaptability or versatility
35.description: Ability of the system to respond to external changes or to perform multiple functions.

36.name: Device complexity
36.description: Number and diversity of elements and interrelations within a system.

37.name: Difficulty of detecting & measuring
37.description: Complexity of measurement and control systems.

38.name: Extent of automation
38.description: Extent to which a system performs its functions without human interface.

39.name: Productivity
39.description: Number of functions or operations performed per unit time.

1.name: Segmentation
1.description: Divide an object into independent parts; make it sectional or easy to disassemble.

2.name: Taking out (Extraction)
2.description: Separate an interfering part or property; extract only the needed part.

3.name: Local quality
3.description: Transition from homogeneous to heterogeneous structure; each part fulfills its specific function.

4.name: Asymmetry
4.description: Change the shape from symmetric to asymmetric; increase the degree of existing asymmetry.

5.name: Merging
5.description: Bring closer together (or merge) identical or related objects, operations, or functions.

6.name: Universality
6.description: Make a part or object perform multiple functions, eliminating the need for other parts.

7.name: Nested doll
7.description: Place one object inside another; pass each object through a cavity of the other.

8.name: Anti-weight
8.description: Compensate the weight of an object by merging with another that provides lift, or by aerodynamic/hydrodynamic forces.

9.name: Preliminary anti-action
9.description: If an action will have both useful and harmful effects, replace it with anti-actions to control harmful effects.

10.name: Preliminary action
10.description: Perform the required change of an object in advance, fully or partially.

11.name: Beforehand cushioning
11.description: Prepare emergency means beforehand to compensate for the relatively low reliability of an object.

12.name: Equipotentiality
12.description: In a potential field, limit position changes (e.g., change the operating conditions to eliminate the need to raise or lower).

13.name: The other way round (Inversion)
13.description: Invert the action used to solve the problem; make movable parts fixed and fixed parts movable.

14.name: Spheroidality / Curvature
14.description: Replace linear parts with curved; replace flat surfaces with spherical; use rollers, balls, spirals.

15.name: Dynamics
15.description: Allow object characteristics, external environment or process to change to be optimal at each operating stage.

16.name: Partial or excessive action
16.description: If 100% of an objective is hard to achieve, achieve somewhat more or less of it; problem may become easier.

17.name: Another dimension
17.description: Move into an additional dimension — from line to plane, from plane to space, multilayer or tilted arrangements.

18.name: Mechanical vibration
18.description: Cause the object to oscillate or vibrate; change frequency, amplitude or use resonance.

19.name: Periodic action
19.description: Replace continuous action with periodic; if action is already periodic, change frequency; use pauses.

20.name: Continuity of useful action
20.description: Carry out work continuously; eliminate idle or intermittent operations.

21.name: Skipping (Hurrying)
21.description: Conduct dangerous or harmful operations at very high speed.

22.name: Blessing in disguise
22.description: Use harmful factors (especially harmful environmental effects) to achieve a positive effect.

23.name: Feedback
23.description: Introduce feedback; if feedback already exists, change its magnitude or influence.

24.name: Intermediary
24.description: Use an intermediary carrier article or intermediate process; merge one object temporarily with another easily removed.

25.name: Self-service
25.description: Make an object serve itself by performing auxiliary helpful functions; use waste resources.

26.name: Copying
26.description: Use simple and inexpensive copies instead of an unavailable, complex, expensive, or fragile object.

27.name: Cheap short-living objects
27.description: Replace an expensive object with a multitude of inexpensive ones, compromising certain qualities.

28.name: Mechanics substitution
28.description: Replace mechanical means with sensory (optical, acoustic, taste, smell); use electric, magnetic, electromagnetic fields.

29.name: Pneumatics and hydraulics
29.description: Use gas and liquid parts in place of solid parts (inflatable, hydrostatic, hydroreactive).

30.name: Flexible shells and thin films
30.description: Use flexible shells and thin films instead of three-dimensional structures; isolate object from environment.

31.name: Porous materials
31.description: Make an object porous or add porous elements; fill the pores with a useful substance.

32.name: Color changes
32.description: Change the color, transparency, or use indicators to improve visibility of an object or process.

33.name: Homogeneity
33.description: Make objects interacting with a primary object of the same material (or with matching properties).

34.name: Discarding and recovering
34.description: Discard portions of an object that have fulfilled their function (dissolve, evaporate); restore consumable parts directly.

35.name: Parameter changes
35.description: Change physical state (gas/liquid/solid), concentration, consistency, temperature, or degree of flexibility.

36.name: Phase transitions
36.description: Use phenomena occurring during phase transitions (volume change, heat absorption/release).

37.name: Thermal expansion
37.description: Use thermal expansion or contraction of materials; combine materials with different coefficients.

38.name: Strong oxidants / Boosted interactions
38.description: Replace common air with oxygen-enriched air, pure oxygen, ionized or ozonized oxygen.

39.name: Inert atmosphere
39.description: Replace a normal environment with an inert one (vacuum, inert gas); add neutral parts or additives.

40.name: Composite materials
40.description: Change from uniform to composite materials combining several properties.
